The timing of this transition, estimated from the inflection point in length-at-age data, is remarkably consistent across individuals, indicating strong canalization of early developmental processes in this epedaphic species.

This longevity estimate, derived from captive cohorts where predation was absent, likely represents an upper bound, as field-based mortality from arthropod predators and desiccation stress would substantially reduce realized lifespans in natural habitats. The asymptotic body size is achieved well before the onset of reproductive senescence, ensuring a prolonged window for egg production.
